# audio_metadata_tool

[← Command index](README.md)

Extract, clear or apply the tags of albums in the local locker's music tree.

## Synopsis

```
audio_metadata_tool [options]
```

## Description

Works on albums: folders of audio files (MP3, M4A, M4B, MP4, AAC) under
`Music/<genre>` in the local locker. A folder that holds sub-folders and no MP3 files
is taken as an artist, and each sub-folder as one of its albums. Without `-g` the
action runs for every genre that has albums.

Actions:

- `Tag` (default): read each album's tags into a JSON file,
  `Audio/Tag/<genre>/[<artist>/]<album>.json` under the file metadata directory. The
  audio files are not changed. Tracks are numbered by their sorted position when they
  have no track number; a missing album is filled in from the folder name and a
  missing album artist from the track artist. The first track's cover art is kept as
  the album's.
- `Apply`: write the tags and cover art from each album's JSON file back into its
  audio files, matching tracks by file name.
- `Clear`: remove the tags from every audio file in each album.

The usual flow is `Tag`, edit the JSON if needed, then `Apply`. `tag_audio_files`
runs both with the settings each genre needs.

## Options

### Selection

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-a, --action <Tag\|Clear\|Apply>` | What to do with each selected album; see the list above. Default: `Tag`. Allowed: `Tag`, `Clear`, `Apply`. |
| `-g, --genre <genre>` | Genre folder under `Music` to work in; every genre with albums when omitted. Allowed: `ASMR`, `Audiobook`, `Classical`, `Game`, `Radio`, `Regular`, `Soundtrack`, `Story`, `Therapy`. |
| `-b, --album <album>` | Name of the one album folder to process; every album in the genre when omitted. |
| `-r, --artist <artist>` | Artist folder that holds the `-b` album, for albums stored as `<artist>/<album>`. |

### Behavior

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `--preserve_artwork` | For `Clear`: keep the embedded cover art. |
| `--clear_existing` | For `Apply`: remove each file's existing tags before writing the ones from the JSON. |
| `--exclude_comments` | For `Tag`: leave comment tags out of the JSON. |
| `--use_index_for_track_number` | For `Tag`: number tracks by their sorted position in the album instead of their existing track numbers. |
| `--set <set>` | For `Tag`: force a tag to a value on every track, as `field=value`; repeat for more fields, e.g. `--set album_artist="Various Artists"`. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Extract the tags of every Soundtrack album to JSON

```bash
audio_metadata_tool -a Tag -g Soundtrack
```

### Extract one album's tags, leaving out comments

```bash
audio_metadata_tool -a Tag -g Regular -b "Some Album" --exclude_comments
```

### Renumber tracks by file order while extracting

```bash
audio_metadata_tool -a Tag -g Audiobook -b "Some Book" --use_index_for_track_number
```

### Force fields to fixed values while extracting

```bash
audio_metadata_tool -a Tag -g Regular -b "Some Album" --set genre=Regular --set album_artist="Various Artists"
```

### Write an album's JSON tags back into its files

```bash
audio_metadata_tool -a Apply -g Soundtrack -b "Some Album"
```

### Preview applying tags without writing anything

```bash
audio_metadata_tool -a Apply -g Soundtrack -b "Some Album" -p -v
```

### Rewrite the tags of the whole library from JSON, dropping any others

```bash
audio_metadata_tool -a Apply --clear_existing
```

### Remove all tags from an album but keep the cover art

```bash
audio_metadata_tool -a Clear -g Regular -b "Some Album" --preserve_artwork
```

### Extract the tags of an album stored under an artist folder

```bash
audio_metadata_tool -a Tag -g Regular -r "Some Artist" -b "Some Album"
```

## Notes

- `Apply` needs the album's JSON file; run `Tag` first. It stops at the first track in the JSON whose file no longer exists, so run `Tag` again after renaming files.
- `--set` is read by `Tag` only. It writes the value to every track and to the album information, overriding what was read from the files and `--use_index_for_track_number`. The field must be one of `title`, `artist`, `album`, `year`, `genre`, `album_artist`, `track_number`, `disc_number`, `bpm`, `key`, `conductor`; an unknown field or a value without `=` stops the tool before anything is read.
- A run over all genres fails if no genre has albums; a genre with no albums is otherwise skipped.
